title: Patient register from a text export
prompt: The registration system exports its patients every night as a `;`-separated file, with birth dates as day/month/year. Write `land()` to put the file in bronze as text and `refine()` to build silver from bronze with real types.
rules: Bronze is the file as it arrived: every column as text, plus `_source_file` with the file's name.
Silver has bronze's columns in the same order, with `birth_date` as a date. Every other column stays text exactly as in the file: a postal code such as `05401` keeps its leading zero.
The export writes an unknown birth date as `00/00/0000`. Those patients are left out of silver.
hints: Read the folder with `spark.read.csv(INCOMING, header=True, sep=";")`. Without a schema or `inferSchema`, every column is text.
`F.try_to_timestamp(col, F.lit("dd/MM/yyyy"))` gives NULL for text that isn't a real date, instead of stopping the job. `.cast("date")` turns it into a date.
To change one column and keep the order, build the `select` list from `bronze.columns`, swapping in the new `birth_date`.
explanation: Bronze reads the file with `header=True` and `sep=";"` and nothing else, so every column is text, and adds `F.lit(FILE).alias("_source_file")`. Silver parses the date with `F.try_to_timestamp(F.col("birth_date"), F.lit("dd/MM/yyyy")).cast("date")`, in a `select` that keeps the other columns as they are, and drops the rows where it's NULL. `00/00/0000` isn't a date: `try_to_timestamp` turns it into NULL, while `F.to_date` stops the job with an error. A `MM/dd` pattern turns 06/12/1957 into 12 June and gives nothing for 27/02. `inferSchema=True` reads postal codes as numbers, so `05401` becomes 5401 and can't be put back: keeping bronze as text is what keeps the file's values intact.
